phase.name: domain_growth
phase.rule: Each PC and named NPC ruler's domain grows according to domain growth rules.

subphase.name: adventuring
subphase.rule: Determine growth triggered by the ruler's adventures occurring in the prior game month.

subphase.name: investment
subphase.rule: Determine growth triggered by agricultural or urban investments made in the prior game month.

subphase.name: random_growth
subphase.rule: Determine growth from fortune and misfortune as +1d10-1d10.

phase.name: congregant_growth
phase.rule: Each divine spellcaster gains 1d10 + Charisma bonus congregants per 1,000gp spent proselytizing during the prior month's campaign activities stage.

phase.name: revenue_collection
phase.rule: Each PC and named NPC ruler collects revenue from domain and urban settlement.

subphase.name: domain_revenue
subphase.rule: Collect land, service, and tax revenue.

subphase.name: urban_revenue
subphase.rule: Collect urban revenue.

subphase.name: tribute
subphase.rule: Collect vassal revenue from loyal vassals.

subphase.name: special_taxes
subphase.rule: Collect special tax revenue from loyal vassals on whom the Tax Demanded duty was imposed or maintained last month.

subphase.name: loans
subphase.rule: Collect loans from loyal vassals on whom the Loan Demanded duty was imposed or maintained last month.

subphase.name: investment_revenue
subphase.rule: Collect revenue from investments made or held last month.

subphase.name: hijink_revenue
subphase.rule: Collect revenue from successful hijinks last month.

subphase.name: favors_and_duties
subphase.rule: Roll for favors and duties imposed by NPC lords on PC vassals.

subphase.name: vagaries_of_recruitment
subphase.rule: Roll for Vagaries of Recruitment for each domain whose ruler is calling up vassal troops, conscripting peasants, hiring mercenaries, levying militia, or soliciting mercenaries this month.

subphase.name: other_vagaries
subphase.rule: Roll for other optional vagaries in use in the campaign.

subphase.name: wandering_monsters
subphase.rule: Make monthly domain encounter throws.

subphase.name: event_allocation
subphase.rule: For each random event scheduled to occur this month, roll 1d4 to determine which week it occurs.

subphase.name: weekly_random_events
subphase.rule: Make weekly domain encounter throws.
For each random event scheduled to occur this week, roll 1d8 to determine which day it occurs; on 8, reroll or choose.
Weekly random events include events carried from the random events phase and events triggered by prior campaign activities, such as arriving mercenaries or interested merchants.

subphase.name: daily_activities
subphase.rule: For each day of the week, make daily domain encounter throws and run that day's activities.

phase.name: second_week
phase.rule: Resolve using the shared week procedure.

phase.name: third_week
phase.rule: Resolve using the shared week procedure.

phase.name: fourth_week
phase.rule: Resolve using the shared week procedure.

phase.name: expense_payment

subphase.name: living_expenses
subphase.rule: Pay PC and NPC living expenses.

subphase.name: hireling_wages
subphase.rule: Pay wages of henchmen, mercenaries, specialists, and other hirelings.

subphase.name: domain_expenses
subphase.rule: Pay domain expenses.

subphase.name: settlement_expenses
subphase.rule: Pay settlement expenses.

subphase.name: congregants
subphase.rule: Pay congregant expenses at 1gp per congregant.
If congregant expenses are not paid, 1d10 congregants depart per 1,000gp left unpaid.

subphase.name: tribute
subphase.rule: Pay tribute owed to lords.

subphase.name: special_taxes
subphase.rule: Pay special tax revenue if a Tax Demanded duty was imposed or maintained on the PC this month.

subphase.name: loans
subphase.rule: Pay loans if a Loan Demanded duty was imposed or maintained on the PC last month.

phase.rule: A ruler may leave one or more expenses unpaid and suffer the appropriate consequences.

phase.name: domain_morale
phase.rule: Resolve domain morale rolls and other domain-morale mechanics.
Starting with the domain with the lowest current morale score, make a domain morale roll for each domain with a PC or named NPC ruler.
Apply modifiers based on taxes, liturgies, campaign activities, and similar effects.

level.name: major
level.rule: Major activities are laborious tasks requiring five to seven hours.

level.name: minor
level.rule: Minor activities are errands or pastimes requiring about one hour or 6 turns.

level.name: trivial
level.rule: Trivial activities require virtually no time.

daily_capacity.rule: Each game day, a character may perform one major activity and two minor activities.
Instead of one major and two minor activities, a character may perform up to eight minor activities.
A character may perform any number of trivial activities.

type.name: singular
type.rule: Takes place within a single game day and may be repeated as often as allowed by available activity slots.

type.name: restricted
type.rule: Takes place within a single game day but cannot be repeated until the stated time period elapses.

type.name: ongoing
type.rule: Requires more than one game day and must be performed throughout the listed time period.
A major ongoing activity represents full-time labor on a complex project or task.
A minor ongoing activity represents intermittent daily effort sustained over a lengthy period.

effort_rules.rule: Activities are either strenuous or unstrenuous.
For every six game days of strenuous activity, a character must rest as the day's major activity for one day.

If required rest is not taken after six days of strenuous activity, the character suffers a cumulative -1 per day penalty to attack throws, damage rolls, and proficiency throws until caught up on required rest.
For campaign play, the turn of rest required after 5 turns of strenuous activity in core ACKS is already factored into what can be accomplished.
Unstrenuous activities do not require rest.

overtime_rules.rule: A character working overtime may perform two major activities, or one major activity and six minor activities, or twelve minor activities in one day.
A day of overtime on unstrenuous activities counts as one day of strenuous activity.
Unstrenuous overtime can be sustained for two days.
Each additional day of unstrenuous overtime thereafter counts as two days of strenuous activity until the character rests.
A day of overtime that includes any strenuous activity counts as three days of strenuous activity.
A day of overtime performing more than eight minor strenuous activities, or one major and two minor strenuous activities, counts as six days of strenuous activity.
Penalties begin on the day after the character exceeds the six-day limit.
Penalties remit at a rate of -1 per day of rest.
A character must rest a minimum of two days or any additional overtime stacks with prior overtime.
For ongoing activities that require a proficiency throw, apply the worst overtime penalty incurred at any point during the process.
A minimum -1 penalty applies to such a throw if the character worked overtime at all, even if careful pacing avoided other penalties.

eligibility_rules.rule: Most campaign activities are open to any character.
Some activities require specific class, level, location, proficiency, or equipment.

activity.name: dungeon_delve
activity.rule: Any character can delve dungeons.
Each 6 turns of exploration counts as one singular strenuous minor activity.
36 turns of exploration counts as one strenuous major activity.

activity.name: fish
activity.requirement: Character must be stationary in a river, lake, or ocean hex.

procedure.step: Attempt a proficiency throw of 14+ on 1d20.
If the character has Survival proficiency, apply +4.
On success, catch enough food to feed 2d6 man-sized creatures for one day.

activity.name: forage
activity.requirement: Character must be in a wilderness hex.
activity.rule: Foraging normally counts as a singular major activity.
A character who travels as a major activity may forage at the same time as a trivial activity.

procedure.step: Attempt a proficiency throw of 18+ on 1d20.
If the character has Survival proficiency, apply +4.
On success, acquire enough food to feed 1d6 man-sized creatures for one day.

activity.name: harvest_parts
activity.requirement: Character must have appropriate proficiencies such as Animal Husbandry, Labor, Trapping, or similar.
activity.rule: Harvesting up to 600gp of special components from one or more creatures counts as a singular strenuous minor activity.
Butchering, skinning, and fleshing up to 180 lbs. worth of creatures counts as a singular strenuous major activity.

activity.name: hunt
activity.requirement: Character must be in a wilderness hex.

procedure.step: Attempt a proficiency throw of 14+ on 1d20.
If the character has Survival proficiency, apply +4.
On success, acquire enough food to feed 2d6 man-sized creatures for one day.
Trigger a wandering monster check from the table appropriate to the terrain.

derived_values.rule: A man-sized creature needs up to 4,000 calories per day of strenuous activity.
1,000 calories of vegetables weighs 1 lb. and costs 1cp; one day's vegetables weigh 4 lbs. and cost 4cp.
A character with Foraging proficiency averages 5cp of food per day.
1,000 calories of meat weighs 1 lb. and costs 4cp; one day's meat weighs 4 lbs. and is worth 16cp.
A character with Hunting proficiency averages 61cp of food per day.
An animal typically yields meat equal to about 40% of body weight in lbs.
Butchering hunted creatures for meat takes 1d6 turns and is included in the hunting activity.

activity.name: rest
activity.rule: Any character can rest.
Resting counts as a singular unstrenuous major activity.
Rest is in addition to normal sleep.
Rest is required to recover from overtime and to recover hit points.
A resting character may still perform two minor activities.
Bed rest is resting overtime; while bed resting, a character may not perform any other activities.
Bed rest is required to recuperate from mortal wounds.

activity.name: search
activity.requirement: Character must be in the wilderness.

procedure.step: Searching one 6-mile hex counts as a strenuous minor activity.
Judge makes a searching throw on behalf of the character or party.
Set target value based on wilderness movement rate.
If the character or a party member has Tracking proficiency, apply +4.
On success, discover one lair in the hex.

activity.name: survey
activity.requirement: Character must have Land Surveying proficiency.
activity.rule: Surveying one 6-mile hex is a minor strenuous activity.
A character searching a hex may survey the same hex as a trivial activity.

procedure.step: Judge secretly makes a proficiency throw.
Base target is 18+.
Apply a cumulative +4 bonus for each successful search the party has conducted in that hex.
If the throw fails with an unmodified 1, reveal an incorrect lair count chosen or rolled by the Judge.
On any other failure, the character does not yet have enough information to make or revise an assessment.

activity.name: trap
activity.requirement: Character must have Trapping proficiency.
activity.rule: Trapping is a singular strenuous minor activity.
Each time the character undertakes the activity, apply 1sp toward the construction cost of a crude trap.
Crude traps cost 1% of the cost of permanent traps.
A crude 10-foot-cube open-earth pit costs 2sp.
A crude 10-foot-cube open-earth pit with spikes costs 12sp.
Crude traps can be found on casual inspection with a successful proficiency throw to find traps, or on deliberate inspection with a +4 bonus.
Crude traps can be removed with a +4 bonus.
Where applicable, crude traps attack at a -2 penalty and provide a +2 bonus to saves to avoid their effects.
After a trap is constructed, it must be managed, which entails checking it for finds, performing minor repairs, and resetting its lures.
Managing any existing trap counts as an ongoing strenuous minor activity per 2sp of construction cost.
Traps set in the wilderness may catch game.

procedure.step: Each day that a trap is managed, make a proficiency throw of 1d20 against a target value of 19+.
On a successful result, the trap yields sufficient food for 1d6 man-sized creatures per 1sp value of the trap.
If the proficiency throw fails with an unmodified 1, the trap breaks completely.
For every six traps being managed, make an encounter throw to see if a wandering monster appropriate for the terrain is in the area.
The monster stumbles into the trap on a throw of 5+ on 1d6; otherwise it is lurking nearby.
1 to 6 traps require one encounter throw, 7 to 12 traps require two encounter throws, 13 to 18 traps require three encounter throws, and so on.

derived_values.rule: A trapper can maintain six 2sp pits with a strenuous major activity each day.
Each such trap has a 10% daily chance of yielding 2d6 x 16cp worth of meat, averaging 11cp each or 66cp total per day.
Each such trap has a 5% daily chance of breaking, so a new trap is needed roughly every three to four days.

activity.name: travel
activity.rule: Traveling 1/8 of the character's long-distance movement rate counts as a singular strenuous minor activity.
Traveling 6/8 of long-distance movement counts as a strenuous major activity.
Terrain slows movement.
Groups move at the rate of the slowest member.
Wilderness travel requires Judge checks for getting lost.
Each time the character or party enters a new wilderness hex, make a wandering monster check.
A character traveling as a major activity may forage as a trivial activity.

category.name: divine
category.rule: Divine activities can only be undertaken by divine spellcasters.

activity.name: dispatch_missionaries
activity.requirement: Divine spellcaster in a domain or settlement with hirelings.
activity.rule: May not be performed more than once per month.
Dispatch hirelings to perform evangelical deeds for a month.
Track the gp value of wages of all hirelings on missionary duty during the month and apply it to next month's congregant growth.

activity.name: cast_charitable_spells
activity.requirement: Divine spellcaster in a domain or settlement.
activity.rule: Cast one or more daily spells for charitable purposes.
Track the gp value of all charitably cast spells using spell costs from the Spell Availability by Market table and apply it to next month's congregant growth.

activity.name: consecrate_altar
activity.requirement: Divine spellcaster level 5+.
activity.rule: An altar consecrated to Chaotic powers creates a sinkhole of evil.
An altar consecrated to Lawful powers creates a pinnacle of good.
The aura size is 100 square feet per 100gp spent on the altar.
Divine power may be spent in lieu of gp if a humbler-looking altar is desired.
Once consecrated, an altar retains its aura until the aura is dispelled or the altar is physically broken and blessed.

activity.name: consecrate_fields
activity.requirement: Divine spellcaster level 5+.

procedure.step: Complete the activity time.
Expend 2gp of divine power per family.
Make a magic research throw.
On success, the fields are consecrated and Land Value increases by 1gp per peasant family during the next month's revenue collection.
On an unmodified 1, the consecration goes awry and Land Value decreases by 1gp per peasant family during the next month's revenue collection.

activity.rule: Fields may be consecrated repeatedly if sufficient divine power is available.

activity.name: consecrate_ruler
activity.requirement: Divine spellcaster level 9+ who is the spiritual advisor of a domain ruler.
activity.rule: May not be performed more than once per year.

procedure.step: Expend divine power equal to the ruler's monthly domain revenue.
Make a magic research throw.

On success, for the next 12 game months the ruler increases base domain morale by 1, gains +1 on all loyalty rolls by vassals, and the Judge rolls twice for vagaries and selects the more favorable result.
On an unmodified 1, the consecration goes awry: base morale decreases by 1, loyalty rolls by vassals take -1, and the ruler suffers the worse of two vagary rolls.

activity.rule: At the Judge's discretion, the magic research throw may be modified by the ruler's behavior in the past 12 months.
For exceptionally impious rulers, awry results may occur on an unmodified 1-3.

activity.name: extract_divine_power
activity.requirement: Divine spellcaster with 50 or more congregants.
activity.rule: May not be performed more than once per week.
Extract 10gp worth of divine power per 50 congregants.
If the caster is the ruler or spiritual advisor of a domain ruler, also extract between 0 and 8 divine power per 10 families in the domain.
Divine power can be spent or accumulated once received.
Under campaign play rules, divine power is not accumulated automatically; the caster must take this activity each week.

activity.name: perform_blood_sacrifice
activity.requirement: Chaotic divine spellcaster.
activity.rule: May not be performed more than once per day.
The spellcaster can conduct one blood sacrifice per class level each time this activity is undertaken.
Each blood sacrifice generates divine power equal to the XP value of the sacrificed creature.
Divine power can be spent or accumulated once received.

activity.name: perform_ceremonial_sacrifice
activity.requirement: Lawful divine spellcaster in a domain or settlement.
activity.rule: May not be performed more than once per day.
Track the gp value of all ceremonial sacrifices performed during the month and apply it to next month's congregant growth.

activity.name: administer_domain
activity.rule: Administering a domain includes holding court, passing laws, standing in judgment, presiding over assemblies, erecting public works, drafting budgets, performing religious ceremonies, and similar tasks.
Rulers who administer their domain gain +1 on domain morale rolls and +5% on domain XP that month.

activity.name: call_to_arms
activity.requirement: Realm ruler.
activity.rule: Each called vassal must muster a force at least equal to 1/2 the garrison of his realm.
Calling for the full garrison counts as demanding two duties and may provoke a Henchman Morale roll.
Arrival time uses weeks, months, or seasons by realm size.
One half of the vassal troops, rounded up, arrive in the first time period after the activity begins.
One quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, arrive in the second time period.
The remainder arrive in the third time period.
The ruler may stop the activity at any time; no more troops arrive thereafter.
1d8 days after the activity begins, and during each monthly random events phase while it continues, roll on Vagaries of Recruitment for the ruler.

activity.name: conscript_troops
activity.requirement: Domain ruler.
activity.rule: Up to 1 conscript per 10 peasant families can be conscripted.
One half of the conscripts, rounded up, arrive in the first week after the activity begins.
One quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, arrive in the second week.
The remainder arrive in the third week.
The ruler may stop the activity at any time; no more conscripts arrive thereafter.
1d8 days after the activity begins, and during each monthly random events phase while it continues, roll on Vagaries of Recruitment for the ruler.

activity.name: consult_senate
activity.requirement: Ruler of a senatorial domain.
activity.rule: A ruler consulting the senate may issue senate-approved decrees as a trivial activity.

activity.name: hire_mercenaries
activity.requirement: Character must have successfully solicited mercenaries.
activity.rule: Offers may be made to individual mercenaries or to formations of companies (120), battalions (500), or brigades (2,000).
Each hiring offer is a singular minor activity.
After the offer is made, make a 2d6 reaction roll on the Reaction to Hiring Offer table.
Every month in which a ruler hires mercenaries, roll on Vagaries of Recruitment for the ruler.

activity.name: inspect_troops
activity.requirement: Character level 5+ with Command proficiency.
activity.rule: Each unit inspected counts as a minor activity.
Inspected troops gain +1 to their first morale roll within one game day.

activity.name: issue_decree
activity.requirement: Domain ruler in his domain.
activity.rule: Issuing a decree is a minor activity, or trivial if the ruler is consulting the senate on that decree.

options.option: Change the rate of taxes or liturgies within the domain.
Grant a favor to a vassal.
Demand a duty of a vassal.
Free a perpetrator caught committing a crime.
Order construction of a new stronghold within the domain.
Order agricultural or urban investment within the domain.

activity.rule: When giving favors, ordering construction, or ordering investment, pay the gp cost immediately.
Judges may instead deduct such costs at 500gp per day.
Morale rolls triggered by demanding duties are rolled immediately.
Funds from taxes or duties are received during the next month's revenue collection.

activity.name: levy_militia
activity.requirement: Domain ruler.
activity.rule: Up to 2 peasants per 10 peasant families can be levied.
One half of the militia, rounded up, arrive in the first week after the activity begins.
One quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, arrive in the second week.
The remainder arrive in the third week.
The ruler may stop the activity at any time; no more militia arrive thereafter.
1d8 days after the activity begins, and during each monthly random events phase while it continues, roll on Vagaries of Recruitment for the ruler.

activity.name: manage_henchmen
activity.rule: A character may actively manage up to four henchmen, plus one additional henchman per point of Charisma bonus and/or Leadership proficiency bonus.
A henchman generally performs any campaign activities he is capable of on behalf of his employer.
The assigned activities may be changed whenever the henchman is accessible physically or magically.
A ruler with henchmen serving as vassal rulers will often need to issue a Call to Counsel decree to bring them to his location to take advantage of this activity.

activity.name: military_campaign
activity.requirement: Character must have an army.
activity.rule: Begins when the character leads troops out of garrison and ends when the troops are returned to garrison or command is handed over.
Resolve daily using campaign procedures; if no opponents are within one week's movement, the Judge may resolve by weeks instead of days.
1d3 game days after the activity begins, and during each weekly random events subphase while the army is on campaign, roll on Vagaries of War for the army.

activity.name: oversee_investment
activity.requirement: Domain ruler in his domain overseeing investment he ordered there.
activity.rule: The investment attracts 1d10+1 new families instead of the usual 1d10 per 1,000gp.

activity.name: oversee_construction
activity.requirement: Domain ruler in his domain overseeing construction there.
activity.rule: A character supervising construction as a major activity may also oversee construction as a trivial activity.
Overseeing increases construction rate by 5%.
If the ruler is also supervising construction, increase construction rate by 10%.

activity.name: oversee_troop_training
activity.requirement: Fighter or other character using fighter attack progression, level 5+, who rules a domain.
activity.rule: Counts as one ongoing minor activity per 60 troops.
Time required depends on troop type and oversight must be maintained throughout the full training time.
A character training troops as a major activity may also oversee those troops as a trivial activity.
Troops whose training is overseen by their domain ruler gain a permanent +1 bonus to morale while they remain in his service.
If the ruler is also training the troops, they finish training as veterans.

activity.name: solicit_mercenaries
activity.rule: A character in an urban settlement may solicit mercenaries from that settlement.
A realm ruler, or a character acting with the ruler's permission, may solicit from the entire realm.
Pay the cost per time period per mercenary type.
One half of the mercenaries, rounded up, arrive in the first time period.
One quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, arrive in the second time period.
The remainder arrive in the third time period.
The activity may be stopped at any time; no more mercenaries arrive thereafter.
1d8 days after a ruler or authorized agent begins soliciting mercenaries, and during each monthly random events phase while it continues, roll on Vagaries of Recruitment for the ruler.

activity.name: supervise_construction
activity.requirement: Character must have sufficient Engineering or Siege Engineering ranks.
activity.rule: Acts as construction supervisor for a project.
A character supervising construction can also oversee construction as a trivial activity.

activity.name: train_troops
activity.requirement: Character must have sufficient Manual at Arms ranks, and Riding and/or Weapon Focus where required.
activity.rule: Train up to 60 troops.
Time required depends on troop type and must be maintained throughout the entire training time.
A character training troops can also oversee those troops as a trivial activity.

activity.name: manage_assistant
activity.requirement: Spellcaster level 9+.
activity.rule: Whenever the spellcaster performs a major magical activity, he may supervise one assistant plus one additional assistant per point of Intelligence bonus as a trivial activity.

activity.name: research_magic
activity.requirement: Appropriate class, level, and necessary equipment.
activity.rule: Magical research includes researching spells, creating magic items, performing ritual spells, creating and designing constructs, creating crossbreeds, and granting unlife.
Duration is days, weeks, or months depending on research type.

activity.name: rewrite_spell
activity.requirement: Arcane spellcaster who has lost his spell book.
activity.rule: Rewrite spells into a new spell book.
Requires 7 days and 1,000gp per spell level.

activity.name: replace_spell
activity.requirement: Arcane spellcaster with a full spell repertoire and a copy of the new spell formula.
activity.rule: Replace one spell in the repertoire with another of equal level.
Replacing a spell does not cause loss of the formula for the replaced spell.
Requires 7 days and 1,000gp per spell level.

activity.name: scribe_spell
activity.requirement: Arcane spellcaster with the spell formula from a scroll or another spellcaster's spell book and able to learn and cast spells of that level.
activity.rule: Scribing from a scroll consumes the scroll.
Scribing from another spellcaster's spell book does not erase the original spell.
Requires 7 days regardless of spell level.

activity.name: buy_sell_equipment
activity.requirement: Character in an urban settlement.
activity.rule: May buy or sell equipment subject to market-class equipment availability limits.

activity.name: buy_sell_magic_items
activity.requirement: Character in an urban settlement.
activity.rule: May buy or sell magic items subject to market-class magic item availability limits.

activity.name: buy_sell_merchandise
activity.requirement: Character with a willing merchant buying or selling merchandise at an acceptable market price.
activity.rule: Each transaction with a merchant counts as a minor activity.
A merchant never buys or sells more than the number of loads rolled.
Loading or unloading costs 1gp per 200 stone of merchandise.
A character selling goods pays customs duty equal to 2d10% of market price.
A character buying and selling in a domain he controls, or smuggling, need not pay customs duties.

activity.name: commission_equipment
activity.requirement: Character in an urban settlement.
activity.rule: A volume of equipment equal to ten times the normal amount available by market class can be commissioned.
Commissioned equipment is not available until complete.
Buildings and vehicles complete at 1 day per 500gp value.
Animal commissions complete at 1 day per 1gp value, or by creature-training rules.
Other equipment commissions complete at 1 day per 5gp value.
Picking up completed equipment counts as a separate minor activity.

activity.name: commission_magic_items
activity.requirement: Character in a Class I market.
activity.rule: Pay up front the base cost, the cost of precious materials, and any required special components.
If the spellcaster successfully completes the item, pay an additional fee equal to 7,000gp per month or twice the base cost, whichever is greater.
Picking up completed magic items counts as a separate minor activity.

activity.name: enter_market
activity.requirement: Character with a caravan or ship of mercantile goods at an urban settlement.
activity.rule: Pay a toll to enter unless sneaking in by smuggling.
Minimum toll is 1gp per load.
While in the market, pay moorage or stabling fees.
Moorage for ships is 1gp per 10 structural hit points per day.
Stabling is 2sp per mule, 5sp per horse, 1gp per cart, and 2gp per wagon per day.
If moorage or stabling is no longer paid, the character has left the market and must pay to re-enter.
Characters buying and selling in their own domain, or smuggling, ignore moorage, stabling, and tolls.

activity.name: hire_hirelings
activity.requirement: Character must have successfully solicited hirelings.
activity.rule: Each hiring offer is a singular minor activity.
After the offer is made, roll 2d6 on the Reaction to Hiring Offer table.

activity.name: persuade_merchants
activity.requirement: Character must have solicited a merchant.
activity.rule: A reaction roll of 9+ is required to persuade a merchant to transact in Common Merchandise.
A reaction roll of 12+ is required to persuade a merchant to transact in Precious Merchandise.
Add the demand modifier when trying to find buyers.
Subtract the demand modifier when trying to find sellers.
If the character has a monopoly over a merchandise type, gain +3 on the roll and merchants buy or sell twice the normal number of loads of that type.
Only one roll per merchant is permitted; on failure, that merchant will not transact with the adventurer.

activity.name: persuade_passengers
activity.requirement: Character must have solicited a passenger.
activity.rule: Make a reaction roll for each passenger.
Only an adjusted 9+ causes the passenger to voyage with the character.
Normal modifiers such as Charisma, Bribery, Diplomacy, Intimidation, Mystic Aura, Seduction, and similar effects apply.

activity.name: persuade_shippers
activity.requirement: Character must have solicited a shipping contract.
activity.rule: Make a reaction roll for each shipper.
Only an adjusted 9+ causes the shipper to move cargo with the character.
Normal modifiers such as Charisma, Bribery, Diplomacy, Intimidation, Mystic Aura, Seduction, and similar effects apply.

activity.name: solicit_hirelings
activity.rule: A character in an urban settlement may solicit hirelings from that settlement.
A realm ruler, or character acting with the ruler's permission, may solicit hirelings from the entire realm.
Pay the cost per time period per hireling type.
One half of the hirelings, rounded up, become interested in the first time period.
One quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, become interested in the second time period.
The remainder become interested in the third time period.
The activity may be stopped at any time; no more hirelings arrive thereafter.

activity.name: solicit_merchants
activity.requirement: Character must have entered a market.
activity.rule: Roll on the merchants column to determine the number of interested merchants, then roll loads for each merchant.
One half of the merchants, rounded up, become interested in the first week.
One quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, become interested in the second week.
The remainder become interested in the third week.
The activity may be stopped early; no more merchants become interested thereafter.
A new solicitation attempt may be made at any time, but the roll takes a cumulative -2 modifier for each week already spent in the market.
A character buying and selling in a domain he controls always gets the maximum number of merchants available.

activity.name: solicit_passengers
activity.requirement: Character must have entered a market.
activity.rule: Determine passenger availability on the Passengers and Shipping Contracts table.
Roll 1d20 to determine each passenger's destination.
On 19+, the passenger wants travel to a distant market of choice 2d20 x 100 miles away.
Otherwise, the passenger wants transport to the closest market within one size class along the adventurer's route.
One half of the passengers, rounded up, become interested in the first week.
One quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, become interested in the second week.
The remainder become interested in the third week.
The activity may be stopped early; no more passengers become interested thereafter.

activity.name: solicit_shipping_contracts
activity.requirement: Character operating a vessel or caravan.
activity.rule: Determine the number and size of available shipping contracts on the Passengers and Shipping Contracts table.
Roll 1d20 to determine the destination of each shipping contract.
On 19+, the shipper wants cargo sent to a distant market of choice 2d20 x 100 miles away.
Otherwise, the shipper wants cargo transported to the closest market within one size class along the adventurer's route.
One half of the shippers, rounded up, become interested in the first week.
One quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, become interested in the second week.
The remainder become interested in the third week.
The activity may be stopped early; no more shippers become interested thereafter.

activity.name: animal_husbandry
activity.requirement: Animal Husbandry proficiency.
activity.rule: Each day, treat three animals plus one additional animal per rank of Animal Husbandry proficiency.
Time required varies with the patients' recovery time.
NPC wages are 1sp + 1sp per proficiency rank per patient per day.

activity.name: create_art_or_craft_goods
activity.requirement: Relevant Artistry or Crafting proficiency.
activity.rule: Duration is determined by construction cost and the character's daily construction rate.
The character may stop early, leaving the art or goods unfinished.
NPC wages equal base construction rate: apprentice 33cp/day, journeyman 66cp/day, master 1gp 33cp/day.

activity.name: gamble
activity.rule: With Gambling proficiency, earn 2 + 6d6 - 3d6 cp per day per proficiency rank.
Without Gambling proficiency, earn 2 + 3d6 - 6d6 cp per day.

procedure.step: Each gambler rolls as if measuring daily gambling income.
Highest total wins the first round.
Losers either exit or increase the bet by rolling again and adding the new roll.
Repeat until no gambler increases the bet.
Highest cumulative total wins; each loser pays the winner the total amount of that loser's rolls.

activity.rule: The stakes may be increased by mutual agreement.

activity.name: heal
activity.requirement: Healing proficiency.
activity.rule: Each day, treat three patients plus one additional patient per additional rank of Healing proficiency.
Time required varies with the patients' recovery time.
NPC wages are 1gp + 1gp per proficiency rank per patient per day.

activity.name: labor
activity.rule: Any character can perform manual labor such as bricklaying or stonecutting.
When laboring directly on a construction project, laboring is a singular strenuous major activity.
When laboring on a construction project, the character provides 1cp per day toward the project's construction rate, or 2cp per day with the appropriate Labor proficiency.
A character may instead hire himself out as a day laborer for wages of 2sp per day.

activity.name: perform
activity.requirement: Relevant Performance proficiency.
activity.rule: NPC fees or tips by rank: apprentice 2d4cp, journeyman 4d4cp, master 8d4cp.
This activity may be undertaken multiple times per day up to the limit of eight minor activities.

activity.name: practice_profession
activity.requirement: Profession proficiency.
activity.rule: NPC wages by rank: apprentice 1gp/day, journeyman 2gp/day, master 4gp/day.

activity.name: supervise_assistants
activity.requirement: Two ranks in an Artistry, Crafting, Performance, or Profession proficiency to supervise up to 2 apprentices.
Three ranks in such a proficiency to supervise up to 2 journeymen and 4 apprentices.
activity.rule: Supervising assistants is a minor ongoing activity, or trivial if the character is working on the same project with them.
Supervised assistants increase their construction rate, or fee/tip if performing, by 50%.
On a large-scale construction project taking more than a day, the supervisor's personal construction rate is reduced by 25%.

activity.name: train_creatures
activity.requirement: Animal Training proficiency appropriate to the creature.
activity.rule: A single trainer can train and manage up to six creatures at once, or work exclusively with one creature throughout its full training.
Duration is determined by the monster's training period and training required.
Common domesticated animals typically require one month plus one month per trick.
NPC wages are monthly and depend on the type of creatures trained.

activity.name: await_trial
activity.rule: Any character caught committing a hijink must await trial in prison.
The character does not roll on the Crime and Punishment table until awaiting trial is complete.
The character may immediately finish awaiting trial by pleading guilty and accepting the lesser punishment.

activity.name: bribe_magistrate
activity.requirement: Bribery proficiency and sufficient funds.
activity.rule: +1 on Crime and Punishment costs 50gp.
+2 costs 350gp.
+3 costs 1,500gp.

activity.name: hire_attorney
activity.rule: May be hired for self or for another caught perpetrator.
Costs 25gp, 50gp, or 100gp and grants +1, +2, or +3 on the caught character's Crime and Punishment roll.

activity.name: interplead
activity.requirement: Domain ruler in the domain where the perpetrator was caught.
activity.rule: Add the ruler's Charisma modifier to the caught character's Crime and Punishment roll.
Add an additional +2 if the interpleader has Diplomacy, Intimidation, or Mystic Aura.
If the ruler controls the domain where the crime occurred, he may instead issue a decree freeing the perpetrator without trial.

activity.name: lay_low
activity.rule: Required after arson, assassination, infiltration, sabotage, smuggling, subversion, or stealing hijinks.
During this time the character may not plan or perform additional hijinks in the same base of operations, but may do so in other bases.
The character does not know how long laying low will take until it is completed.
If the character does not lay low, then on the next hijink in that base he is caught if the proficiency throw fails by 11 or more or is an unmodified 1-3.
Other hijinks do not require laying low.

activity.name: order_hijink
activity.requirement: Boss of a syndicate.
activity.rule: Assigning hijinks to any and all syndicate members at the boss's base counts as a singular major activity.
Assigning hijinks to a syndicate controlled by an underboss counts as a separate singular major activity.
Assigning hijinks to a small number of members, 1/6 of the syndicate membership or less, counts as a singular minor activity.
By custom, a boss assigns each member one hijink per month and leaves the completion deadline within that month to the perpetrator.
Assigning additional hijinks or imposing a deadline triggers a loyalty roll by the member.

activity.name: plan_hijink
activity.requirement: Appropriate thief skill necessary to perform the hijink.
activity.rule: Required for arson, assassination, infiltration, sabotage, smuggling, subversion, and stealing hijinks to avoid penalties.
Perpetrators level 5+ plan in 2d6+3 days.
Perpetrators level 9+ plan in 2d4+3 days.
The perpetrator does not know the required planning time until planning is completed.
If the hijink is performed before planning is complete, apply -1 to the proficiency throw per day of incomplete planning.
The penalty is revealed when the die roll is made.
A hijink may be planned on behalf of another perpetrator.
Hijinks outside the listed set neither require nor benefit from planning.

activity.name: perform_hijink
activity.requirement: Appropriate thief skill.
activity.rule: Hijinks that can be planned - arson, assassination, escaping, infiltration, sabotage, smuggling, and stealing - are singular unstrenuous major activities requiring 1 day.
Other hijinks - carousing, disinforming, slandering, spying, and treasure hunting - are ongoing unstrenuous major activities requiring 3d6+10 days.
Perpetrators level 5+ perform ongoing hijinks in 3d4+8 days.
Perpetrators level 9+ perform ongoing hijinks in 2d6+5 days.
The perpetrator does not know required time for an ongoing hijink until it is completed.
When the activity is complete, make the hijink throw.
If the hijink is rushed, apply -1 to the proficiency throw per day of incomplete activity.
The penalty is revealed when the die roll is made.
